biography: Luiz Otávio Floss, a name whispered with respect and a hint of caution in the Brazilian racing circles, didn't come from racing royalty. Born in Curitiba, his early life revolved around his father's small auto repair shop. Luiz wasn't initially drawn to speed, but rather to the intricate mechanics, spending hours disassembling and reassembling engines. His racing debut came unexpectedly at 22, filling in for an injured driver in a local karting event. He surprised everyone, including himself, with a natural talent and an uncanny ability to read the track. The turning point was the 2015 Stock Car Brasil season, where he secured three podiums, catching the eye of Sigma P1. Now, nearing 40, Luiz is a seasoned veteran, a calculating strategist who leverages his experience to outmaneuver younger, more aggressive drivers. While a championship title has eluded him, he remains a formidable competitor, driven by a quiet determination and a deep understanding of the machinery beneath him.
drivingStyle: Luiz's driving style is best described as 'precise calculation'. He's not one for flamboyant overtakes or daring dives. Instead, he meticulously studies the track, analyzing every corner and apex. He's a master of tire management, nursing his rubber through long stints while maintaining a consistently competitive pace. Luiz excels under pressure, rarely cracking under the weight of expectation. He prefers to let the race come to him, patiently waiting for opportunities to capitalize on his rivals' mistakes.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision in the 2018 Interlagos race. Esteves blamed Luiz for the incident, leading to heated exchanges and aggressive on-track battles ever since.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2017 Curitiba Grand Prix in front of his home crowd. After starting in 8th position, he executed a brilliant strategy to conserve his tires and overtake his rivals in the closing laps.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2020 São Paulo Grand Prix due to a mechanical failure. The incident cost him a potential championship victory.
